# Does the full moon cause more births?

**Verdict:** ✅ Estimated from data

## What the research and analysis found

The evidence does not support the idea that the full moon causes more births. Our estimate from U.S. birth records found no evidence of an effect, with an adjusted mean difference of 19.31 births (95% CI -85.48 to 124.10). [res-b4b0aa6a] Published studies point in different directions: several large studies found no link between lunar phases and birth rates, while a few reported small increases around the full moon. [s32c5b4a7-effect, sbeac1891-effect, s37306091-effect, sf3162a4c-effect, s437ceecc-effect, s424ad64d-effect, s082899d5-effect, s1b12df01-effect, s86a5a73a-effect, sabee61d7-effect, sa80967f0-effect, s0ca7a4e6-effect, s14433d26-effect, sdea1f1b5-effect, s86b44ac2-effect, s9dc3505a-effect, sd76b98e6-effect] Because the best studies conflict and the data are observational, certainty is very low.

## Question (PECO)

- **Population:** pregnant people giving birth in hospitals
- **Exposure:** the night of the full moon, defined as the moment when the Moon is fully illuminated as seen from Earth
- **Comparator:** any other night (not the full moon)
- **Outcome:** the number of live births occurring in a hospital during a 24-hour period
- **Time window:** the 24 hours following the moment of full moon
- **Estimand:** ATE, mean difference, deviations handled n/a

## Causal graph (DAG)

- full_moon → births: the question being tested
- full_moon → moonlight: assumed (no source)
- moonlight → births: cites sdea1f1b5-effect
- day_of_week → births: assumed (no source)
- holiday → births: cites s9dc3505a-effect
- season → births: cites s424ad64d-effect
- year → births: assumed (no source)

Treated as exogenous (the model's judgment that nothing in the graph can cause it; no source): full_moon, day_of_week, holiday, season, year.

## Key confounders

No confounder in the DAG.

Adjusted for: nothing.

## Evidence

**Certainty:** very low (starts low: best evidence is observational; down one: best studies point in different directions (+, null))

Evidence flow: 74 sources found → 60 studies after dedupe → 32 included (excluded: wrong_population 4, not_a_study 4, off_topic 15, wrong_outcome 5).

Europe PMC lookups failed for 10 queries (after one retry): the studies they were for may lack a DOI or PMID and were not checked for retraction.

- [No evidence of purported lunar effect on hospital admission rates or birth rates.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4418782) — cross_sectional, 2015: did not correlate in any way with the cycle of lunar phases
- [The Impact of Lunar Phases During Day and Night Cycles on Perinatal Outcomes: A Nationwide Cohort Study.](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12894514) — cohort, 2026: SBR: 1.0000 (95% CI: 0.9844–1.0000)
- [The Effect of Lunar Cycle on the Frequency of Birth in Al-Elwiya Maternity Hospital, Baghdad, 2017](https://www.ijmrhs.com/abstract/the-effect-of-lunar-cycle-on-the-frequency-of-birth-in-alelwiya-maternity-hospital-baghdad-2017-14834.html) — cohort, 2017: increase in the percentage of deliveries in the Waning Gibbous (15.64%) and the full moon (14.70%)
- [Novel perspectives on the influence of the lunar cycle on the timing of full-term human births.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32703035) — cohort, 2020: the number of births varied in relation specifically to the changing amount of moonlight during the nighttime at different stages of the lunar cycle, with highest number of births at or around the time of the full moon
- [The effect of the lunar cycle on frequency of births and birth complications.](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/15902138) — cohort, 2005: no significant differences in the frequency of births ... across the 8 phases of the moon or between documented high- and low-volume intervals of the lunar cycle
- [Exploring the mystical relationship between the Moon, Sun, and birth rate.](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12884-024-06654-1) — cohort, 2024: We found no evidence that moonlight has any role in the birth prevalence rate
- [Influence of the lunar cycle on birthrates](https://english.elpais.com/health/2024-03-30/does-the-moon-play-a-role-in-childbirth.html) — cross_sectional, 2004, known only from secondary sources: there were no significant differences in the total number of deliveries nor in any of the groups that were analyzed

## Estimate

Adjusted mean difference: 19.31 (95% CI -85.48 to 124.10), OLS, HC1 robust SEs.

Unadjusted: -10.46 (95% CI -342.96 to 322.03).

Confounders adjusted for: none (no backdoor path in the DAG).
Also adjusted for, to narrow the CI: day_of_week, holiday, season, year.

3652 rows used (123 exposed).

In the data: `full_moon` ← `full_moon(date)`; `births` ← `births`; `day_of_week` ← `day_of_week (categories)`; `holiday` ← `holiday(date)`; `season` ← `season(month)`; `year` ← `year`

## Comparison with published

Our estimate of 19.31 more births on full-moon nights is in the same positive direction as some published findings, such as the very small (+0.4%) surplus in a French analysis of 38.7 million births, but its confidence interval includes no effect. [res-b4b0aa6a, s9dc3505a-effect]

## Limitations

- Certainty is very low because the best evidence is observational and the best studies point in different directions.
- The column mapping for the U.S. birth data was not confirmed by the user.
- The analysis assumes no unmeasured confounding after adjusting for nothing, which may miss confounders the DAG does not include.
- The data are observational, with no randomization documented.
